To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the pattern of quality-based versus cost-based competence varies across sectors and across export versus domestic sales, and (ii) the pattern of competence is driven by firms' incentives to improve the perceived value of products, rather than by their cost of production.

The quality-based competence hypothesis predicts that the prices of differentiated products will fall with distance from a firm's core competence, while the cost-based competence hypothesis predicts the opposite.
